children.text: Ray tracing and generation of entangled light

For a plane wave in a nonmagnetic dielectric use \(\mathbf B=\mu_0\mathbf H\), \(\mathbf k\times\mathbf E=\omega\mathbf B\), \(\mathbf k\times\mathbf H=-\omega\mathbf D\), energy density \(u=(\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf D+\mathbf H\cdot\mathbf B)/2\) and Poynting vector S=E×H. Ray speed is |S|/u. In A take D=εE. In B the optic axis is z and D=(εEx,εEy,ε′Ez), with no=c√(μ0ε), ne=c√(μ0ε′). Initially k=k(sinθ,0,cosθ). A signed angle from E to D, or from S to k, is positive clockwise in the source xz view. For refraction the interface is yz, incident medium isotropic with index n, and the crystal axes x2,z2 are rotated by φ as shown. In C a nonzero quadratic polarization \(P_i^{NL}=\sum_{jk}\chi^{(2)}_{ijk}E_jE_k\) couples three waves. Positive frequencies satisfy ω≥ω2 and ω1≥ω2. Use photon energy ℏω and momentum ℏk. The specified entangled pair is \((|x'_ay'_b\rangle+|y'_ax'_b\rangle)/\sqrt2\). Linear polarizers at a,b have axes at α,β measured from x′, and perpendicular settings add π/2.
Find vp in terms of ε and μ0.
Find the energy-flow direction and ray speed.
Find all permissible D and B directions and indices for k in xz. Identify directions with only one index.
Find normalized E directions, identify ordinary and extraordinary waves, and give tanα.
Extend the modes to arbitrary k̂ making angle θ with z.
Find tanαr,vr,Ŝ for both modes and express ray index ns=c/vr through Ŝ.

children.text: Ray tracing and generation of entangled light
Eliminate B,H from Maxwell equations. With k·E=0, k²E=ω²μ0εE. Thus \(v_p=\omega/k=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon}\).
E,H,k are mutually orthogonal and E×H points along k. The electric and magnetic energy densities are equal, so u=|S|/vp. Thus Ŝ=k̂ and vr=vp=1/√(μ0ε).

The ordinary mode has D̂=±ŷ, B̂=±(−cosθ,0,sinθ) and n=no. The extraordinary mode has D̂=±(cosθ,0,−sinθ), B̂=±ŷ with correlated signs and \[n(\theta)=\frac{n_on_e}{\sqrt{n_o^2\sin^2\theta+n_e^2\cos^2\theta}}.\] At θ=0 or π both indices equal no. For a genuinely anisotropic crystal these are the optic-axis directions.

The ordinary mode has Ê=±ŷ and α=0. The extraordinary direction is \[\hat E=\pm\frac{(n_e^2\cos\theta,0,-n_o^2\sin\theta)}{\sqrt{n_e^4\cos^2\theta+n_o^4\sin^2\theta}}.\] Comparing slopes of E and D gives \[\tan\alpha=\frac{(n_o^2-n_e^2)\tan\theta}{n_e^2+n_o^2\tan^2\theta}.\] Overall sign of polarization is immaterial.

Let \(\hat t=(\hat k-\cos\theta\hat z)/\sin\theta\). The same two indices apply. Ordinary Ê is ±(k̂×ẑ)/sinθ. Extraordinary Ê is proportional to \(n_e^2\cos\theta\hat t-n_o^2\sin\theta\hat z\), normalized as in B2. At sinθ=0 choose any two transverse orthogonal polarizations, since the modes are degenerate. This vector form avoids the inconsistent expanded z coefficient printed in one source formula.

Ordinary light has αr=0, vr=c/no and Ŝ=k̂. For extraordinary light αr=α, and with \(D=n_e^2\cos^2\theta+n_o^2\sin^2\theta\), \(W=\sqrt{n_e^4\cos^2\theta+n_o^4\sin^2\theta}\), \[\hat S=(n_o^2\sin\theta,0,n_e^2\cos\theta)/W,\qquad v_r=\frac{cW}{n_on_e\sqrt D}=v_p/\cos\alpha_r.\] The extraordinary ray index is \(n_s=\sqrt{n_e^2(\hat S\cdot\hat x)^2+n_o^2(\hat S\cdot\hat z)^2}\). For ordinary light ns=no.

Write s=n sinθ1. Differentiating optical travel time at the interface gives \(s^2=(P_3-P_1\tan\theta_2)^2/(P_1\tan^2\theta_2-2P_3\tan\theta_2+P_2)\). Therefore \[A=P_1(s^2-P_1),\quad\bar B=-2P_3(s^2-P_1),\quad C=P_2s^2-P_3^2.\] Select the root consistent with the unsquared Fermat equation and forward energy flow. At φ=0, \(\tan\theta_2=n_es/[n_o\sqrt{n_o^2-s^2}]\). At φ=π/2, \(\tan\theta_2=n_os/[n_e\sqrt{n_e^2-s^2}]\).

Products of plane-wave phases yield sum and difference components. Matching gives \(\omega=\omega_1\pm\omega_2\), \(\mathbf k=\mathbf k_1\pm\mathbf k_2\), with consistent signs. Multiplication by ℏ gives energy and momentum conservation. Decay of the pump photon uses \(\omega=\omega_1+\omega_2\) and \(\mathbf k=\mathbf k_1+\mathbf k_2\).

The same-polarization channels o→o+o and e→e+e are impossible. Their parent index at the larger frequency exceeds either daughter index, while momentum matching would require a frequency-weighted average of the daughter indices. No cross-polarization channel is universally excluded without additional information relating no and ne.

Put ν=Ω−Ωe, so Ω−Ωo=−ν. The ordinary longitudinal component is \(k_{2z}=K_o-
u/u_o-q^2/(2K_o)\). The source angular approximation gives \(k_{1z}=K_e+
u/u_e+N_eq_{x'}+[N_e\cot	heta-1]q^2/(2K_e)\). Sum these and impose Kp=Ke+Ko. Completing the square gives \[M= rac{K_o(1-N_e\cot	heta)+K_e}{2K_eK_o},\quad N=- rac{N_e}{2M},\quad L=-
u(1/u_o-1/u_e)+ rac{N_e^2}{4M}.\] The centre is qx′=−N. Its tilt magnitude is |N|/Ko and cone half-angle is √(L/M)/Ko, provided L≥0. Signs describe the chosen x′ direction. The source changes coefficient letters mid-derivation and has some dimensional typos in its final angle formula. These expressions follow its stated longitudinal expansion. A general expansion retaining curvature of ne(θ) requires further second angular derivatives.

The joint transmission amplitude is (cosαsinβ+sinαcosβ)/√2. Squaring gives \[P(\alpha,\beta)=P(\alpha_\perp,\beta_\perp)=\tfrac12\sin^2(\alpha+\beta),\] \[P(\alpha,\beta_\perp)=P(\alpha_\perp,\beta)=\tfrac12\cos^2(\alpha+\beta).\] The field checks P(α,β).

The four normalized joint probabilities give \(E=-\cos[2(\alpha+\beta)]\). Therefore S is the indicated absolute-value combination of these cosines with sums of angles. At the specified settings S=2√2>2. The source incorrectly simplifies its own C4 probabilities to a difference of angles in one line, but both the consistent sum convention and a reversed b-axis convention give the same S for these settings. The field checks the numerical S.

solution.text:
Ray tracing and generation of entangled light
a.1. Isotropic phase speed
Eliminate B,H from Maxwell equations. With k·E=0, k²E=ω²μ0εE. Thus \(v_p=\omega/k=1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon}\).
a.2. Isotropic index
By n=c/vp, \(n=c\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon}\).
a.3. Isotropic ray
E,H,k are mutually orthogonal and E×H points along k. The electric and magnetic energy densities are equal, so u=|S|/vp. Thus Ŝ=k̂ and vr=vp=1/√(μ0ε).
b.1. Uniaxial eigenmodes
The ordinary mode has D̂=±ŷ, B̂=±(−cosθ,0,sinθ) and n=no. The extraordinary mode has D̂=±(cosθ,0,−sinθ), B̂=±ŷ with correlated signs and \[n(\theta)=\frac{n_on_e}{\sqrt{n_o^2\sin^2\theta+n_e^2\cos^2\theta}}.\] At θ=0 or π both indices equal no. For a genuinely anisotropic crystal these are the optic-axis directions.
b.2. Polarizations and walk-off angle
The ordinary mode has Ê=±ŷ and α=0. The extraordinary direction is \[\hat E=\pm\frac{(n_e^2\cos\theta,0,-n_o^2\sin\theta)}{\sqrt{n_e^4\cos^2\theta+n_o^4\sin^2\theta}}.\] Comparing slopes of E and D gives \[\tan\alpha=\frac{(n_o^2-n_e^2)\tan\theta}{n_e^2+n_o^2\tan^2\theta}.\] Overall sign of polarization is immaterial.
b.3. Arbitrary propagation azimuth
Let \(\hat t=(\hat k-\cos\theta\hat z)/\sin\theta\). The same two indices apply. Ordinary Ê is ±(k̂×ẑ)/sinθ. Extraordinary Ê is proportional to \(n_e^2\cos\theta\hat t-n_o^2\sin\theta\hat z\), normalized as in B2. At sinθ=0 choose any two transverse orthogonal polarizations, since the modes are degenerate. This vector form avoids the inconsistent expanded z coefficient printed in one source formula.
b.4. Extraordinary energy flow
Ordinary light has αr=0, vr=c/no and Ŝ=k̂. For extraordinary light αr=α, and with \(D=n_e^2\cos^2\theta+n_o^2\sin^2\theta\), \(W=\sqrt{n_e^4\cos^2\theta+n_o^4\sin^2\theta}\), \[\hat S=(n_o^2\sin\theta,0,n_e^2\cos\theta)/W,\qquad v_r=\frac{cW}{n_on_e\sqrt D}=v_p/\cos\alpha_r.\] The extraordinary ray index is \(n_s=\sqrt{n_e^2(\hat S\cdot\hat x)^2+n_o^2(\hat S\cdot\hat z)^2}\). For ordinary light ns=no.
b.5. Fermat refraction quadratic
Write s=n sinθ1. Differentiating optical travel time at the interface gives \(s^2=(P_3-P_1\tan\theta_2)^2/(P_1\tan^2\theta_2-2P_3\tan\theta_2+P_2)\). Therefore \[A=P_1(s^2-P_1),\quad\bar B=-2P_3(s^2-P_1),\quad C=P_2s^2-P_3^2.\] Select the root consistent with the unsquared Fermat equation and forward energy flow. At φ=0, \(\tan\theta_2=n_es/[n_o\sqrt{n_o^2-s^2}]\). At φ=π/2, \(\tan\theta_2=n_os/[n_e\sqrt{n_e^2-s^2}]\).
c.1. Phase matching
Products of plane-wave phases yield sum and difference components. Matching gives \(\omega=\omega_1\pm\omega_2\), \(\mathbf k=\mathbf k_1\pm\mathbf k_2\), with consistent signs. Multiplication by ℏ gives energy and momentum conservation. Decay of the pump photon uses \(\omega=\omega_1+\omega_2\) and \(\mathbf k=\mathbf k_1+\mathbf k_2\).
c.2. Forbidden collinear channels
The same-polarization channels o→o+o and e→e+e are impossible. Their parent index at the larger frequency exceeds either daughter index, while momentum matching would require a frequency-weighted average of the daughter indices. No cross-polarization channel is universally excluded without additional information relating no and ne.
c.3. Down-conversion cones
Put ν=Ω−Ωe, so Ω−Ωo=−ν. The ordinary longitudinal component is \(k_{2z}=K_o-\nu/u_o-q^2/(2K_o)\). The source angular approximation gives \(k_{1z}=K_e+\nu/u_e+N_eq_{x'}+[N_e\cot\theta-1]q^2/(2K_e)\). Sum these and impose Kp=Ke+Ko. Completing the square gives \[M=\frac{K_o(1-N_e\cot\theta)+K_e}{2K_eK_o},\quad N=-\frac{N_e}{2M},\quad L=-\nu(1/u_o-1/u_e)+\frac{N_e^2}{4M}.\] The centre is qx′=−N. Its tilt magnitude is |N|/Ko and cone half-angle is √(L/M)/Ko, provided L≥0. Signs describe the chosen x′ direction. The source changes coefficient letters mid-derivation and has some dimensional typos in its final angle formula. These expressions follow its stated longitudinal expansion. A general expansion retaining curvature of ne(θ) requires further second angular derivatives.
c.4. Coincidence probabilities
The joint transmission amplitude is (cosαsinβ+sinαcosβ)/√2. Squaring gives \[P(\alpha,\beta)=P(\alpha_\perp,\beta_\perp)=\tfrac12\sin^2(\alpha+\beta),\] \[P(\alpha,\beta_\perp)=P(\alpha_\perp,\beta)=\tfrac12\cos^2(\alpha+\beta).\] The field checks P(α,β).
c.5. CHSH violation
The four normalized joint probabilities give \(E=-\cos[2(\alpha+\beta)]\). Therefore S is the indicated absolute-value combination of these cosines with sums of angles. At the specified settings S=2√2>2. The source incorrectly simplifies its own C4 probabilities to a difference of angles in one line, but both the consistent sum convention and a reversed b-axis convention give the same S for these settings. The field checks the numerical S.
